title: Uni-Mol screening guides experimental validation of β-sheet tetrapeptide assemblies
summary: A fine-tuned Uni-Mol model used simulation-derived data to screen 160,000 tetrapeptides. Researchers experimentally tested 26 selected tetrapeptide candidates: 15 formed β-sheet assemblies, including seven hydrogelators, as assessed with structural and assembly assays. The study reports experimental validation across 46 candidates overall; the 15/26 result is specific to the screened tetrapeptide set. This is a materials-science preprint, not evidence of medical function or clinical use. A related 2023 study explored tetrapeptide hydrogelation; this record makes no claim that every sequence is unprecedented and is limited to the present paper’s β-sheet structural validation.
ai_technology: Fine-tuned Uni-Mol machine-learning model for Amyloid-Like Tendency prediction, guided by hybrid-resolution molecular-dynamics simulations

source_review.scope: ChemRxiv v1 page, full manuscript and Supplementary Information; official bioRxiv API metadata/abstract for cited 2025 computational preprint; primary 2023 hydrogel paper and linked supplementary-data index. Full-text source limits and the bounded result are stated.

evidence.tested: In the Uni-Mol-screened tetrapeptide set, 26 candidates were experimentally characterized; 15 formed β-sheet assemblies and seven were reported as hydrogelators. The authors also report validation of 46 candidates across the study overall.
evidence.unknown: The 46-candidate set combines tripeptide and tetrapeptide validations; the 15/26 result is specific to the tetrapeptides. The work is a preprint and establishes laboratory assembly outcomes only, not biomedical function, clinical utility, or independent replication. No claim is made that every sequence is unprecedented.
evidence.ai_role: Uni-Mol was fine-tuned on simulation-derived data and used to screen 160,000 tetrapeptides for Amyloid-Like Tendency; predictions guided candidate selection for further simulation and experimental structural characterization.
